heroHeadline: Solar Becomes EU's Largest Power Source; Amazon Deforestation at Decade Low; Global EV Sales Top 2 Million for First Time
heroSubtitle: 3,869 days since the Paris Agreement — Ember confirmed (July 14) that solar generated a record 52 TWh of EU electricity in June 2026, a 25% monthly share that made it the bloc's single largest power source for the first time, ahead of nuclear, gas, wind, hydro and coal. Brazilian government data (July 10) showed Amazon deforestation fell to its lowest first-half total in a decade — 1,295 km² from January-June, down 38% year-on-year. Global EV sales hit 2.0 million units in June 2026 (July 9, Rho Motion/Benchmark Mineral Intelligence) — the first calendar month ever above 2 million, with Europe posting an all-time monthly record. Earlier in the month, Washington signed a historic carbon market linkage with California and Québec (June 25), and the UNFCCC's Bonn SB64 talks (June 8-18) closed in gridlock on adaptation finance while advancing a just-transition mechanism package for COP31 in Antalya.
footerNote: Data sourced from IEA, IRENA, Ember, BloombergNEF, Rho Motion, UNFCCC, and major international outlets. All figures reflect verified, publicly available data through July 2026.
